title: IREB CPRE Foundation Level
summary: The internationally recognized entry-level certification in requirements engineering, aligned to the IREB syllabus.
description:
The CPRE Foundation Level is the internationally recognized starting point for a career in requirements engineering. This course covers the full IREB syllabus — requirements elicitation, documentation, validation, and management — and prepares you for the official CPRE Foundation Level exam.

You'll leave with a practical, standards-based vocabulary for requirements work, and the confidence to apply it on real projects the following week.
outcomes: Explain the purpose and scope of requirements engineering within a project
Apply elicitation techniques suited to different stakeholder situations
Write unambiguous, verifiable requirements using structured templates (including EARS)
Distinguish functional, non-functional, and constraint requirements
Understand the fundamentals of requirements management and change control

title: IREB CPRE Advanced Level — Elicitation
summary: Deepen your elicitation practice — advanced stakeholder analysis, negotiation, and conflict resolution.
description: Building on Foundation Level knowledge, this Advanced Level course focuses entirely on elicitation: how to draw out real needs from stakeholders who don't always know how to articulate them, resolve conflicting requirements, and run elicitation at scale across distributed teams.
outcomes: Select and justify elicitation techniques for complex stakeholder landscapes
Facilitate structured negotiation between conflicting stakeholder needs
Design an elicitation strategy for a multi-team, multi-site project

title: IREB CPRE Advanced Level — Requirements Modeling
summary: Model requirements with precision using UML, BPMN, and goal-oriented notations.
description: This Advanced Level course teaches you to represent requirements as models where text alone falls short — process flows, state behavior, and system context — using industry-standard notations that hold up under review and change.
outcomes: Choose the right modeling notation for a given requirement type
Build clear, consistent UML and BPMN models from natural-language input
Review models for completeness and consistency against source requirements

topics: When to model vs. when to write text

title: IREB CPRE Advanced Level — Requirements Management
summary: Traceability, change control, and requirements governance for long-lived, evolving projects.
description: Requirements rarely stay still. This course covers how to manage them properly once they exist — traceability across the lifecycle, controlled change, versioning, and the governance practices that keep a large or long-running project's requirements trustworthy.
outcomes: Design a traceability scheme appropriate to project risk and regulation
Run a controlled requirements change process
Set up requirements governance for a multi-release product

title: RE@Agile
summary: Practical requirements engineering discipline inside Scrum and Kanban teams — without the heavyweight process.
description: Agile doesn't remove the need for good requirements — it changes how they're captured and evolved. This course teaches you to bring real RE discipline (clarity, traceability, verifiability) into backlogs, user stories, and sprint-based delivery, without reintroducing the overhead agile teams push back against.
outcomes: Write user stories that are both agile-friendly and genuinely verifiable
Maintain lightweight traceability across sprints without heavyweight tooling
Facilitate backlog refinement sessions that surface real requirements gaps

title: AI4RE Microcredential
summary: Use AI responsibly to accelerate elicitation, drafting, and quality review — without losing rigor.
description: A focused, single-day microcredential on applying AI tools to requirements engineering work — drafting, quality-checking, and translating between formats — while keeping the discipline's own standards (IREB CPRE, EARS) firmly in the driver's seat, not the AI.
outcomes: Use AI tools to accelerate first-draft requirement writing without sacrificing quality
Apply IREB CPRE quality criteria to review AI-assisted output critically
Recognize where AI assistance helps and where it introduces real risk

topics: Where it helps, where it doesn't
Applying CPRE criteria as a check

title: Introduction to Systems Engineering
summary: The fundamentals of systems thinking, lifecycle processes, and INCOSE/ISO 15288 practice.
description: A practical introduction to systems engineering for anyone who needs to understand how complex systems get built — lifecycle processes, systems thinking, and how requirements, architecture, and verification connect across a program.
outcomes: Explain the systems engineering lifecycle per ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288
Apply systems thinking to decompose a complex problem into a coherent architecture
Understand how requirements, design, and verification stay connected across a program

title: Complete System Analysis (INCOSE + ISO 15288)
summary: A comprehensive treatment of system analysis practice aligned to INCOSE and ISO 15288.
description: A deeper program for engineers who need to run system analysis end to end — stakeholder needs, requirements, functional analysis, and architecture trade-offs — grounded in INCOSE practice and ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288.
outcomes: Run a complete stakeholder-needs-to-requirements analysis for a complex system
Perform functional analysis and allocate requirements to architecture
Apply trade-off analysis techniques to competing architectural options

title: Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Fundamentals
summary: Move from document-based to model-based systems engineering practice with SysML.
description: An applied introduction to MBSE — why model-based practice reduces ambiguity and rework, and how to actually get started with SysML on a real program, not just in theory.
outcomes: Explain the case for MBSE over document-centric systems engineering
Build core SysML diagrams (block definition, requirements, activity)
Plan an MBSE adoption path for an existing document-based program

title: Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP) Prep
summary: Comprehensive exam preparation for IIBA's senior-level business analysis certification.
description: Full-syllabus preparation for the CBAP exam, covering all six BABOK knowledge areas, with practice questions and exam strategy from instructors who've supported candidates through the real thing.
outcomes: Navigate all six BABOK knowledge areas confidently
Apply BA techniques to realistic exam-style scenarios
Build a personal study and exam-day strategy

topics: All six areas, mapped to the exam blueprint

title: Certification of Capability in Business Analysis (CCBA) Prep
summary: IIBA's mid-level BA certification, for practitioners with a few years of hands-on experience.
description: Exam preparation for the CCBA certification, aimed at business analysts with 2-3 years of experience who are ready to formalize their practice against the BABOK.
outcomes: Map real project experience against BABOK knowledge areas
Apply core BA techniques correctly in exam scenarios
Prepare a realistic study plan for the CCBA exam

title: Requirements Elicitation Workshop
summary: A hands-on, single-day workshop on running effective requirements elicitation sessions.
description: A practical, workshop-format day focused entirely on the craft of elicitation — interviewing, facilitation, and getting to real needs, not just stated wants.
outcomes: Run a structured stakeholder interview that surfaces real needs
Facilitate a requirements workshop with a mixed-seniority group
Recognize and probe past superficial or contradictory stakeholder statements

title: Bulletproof Business Cases
summary: Build business cases that survive scrutiny from finance, leadership, and skeptical stakeholders.
description: A practical course on constructing business cases that hold up — realistic cost/benefit analysis, risk framing, and the storytelling that gets a good case actually approved.
outcomes: Structure a business case that withstands financial scrutiny
Frame risk and assumptions honestly without undermining the case
Present a business case persuasively to senior stakeholders

title: ASPICE Fundamentals
summary: The foundations of Automotive SPICE — process assessment, SWE processes, and traceability.
description: A foundational course in Automotive SPICE for teams working with or being assessed against ASPICE — process structure, key SWE processes, and the traceability evidence assessors actually look for.
outcomes: Explain the ASPICE process reference and assessment models
Identify the traceability evidence required across SWE.1-SWE.6
Prepare for an internal ASPICE readiness review

title: Software-Defined Vehicles (SDV)
summary: What SDV architecture means for requirements, systems engineering, and organizational practice.
description: An engineering-track overview of software-defined vehicle architecture and what it changes about requirements engineering, systems engineering, and release practice in automotive organizations moving away from fixed ECU-per-function designs.
outcomes: Explain the architectural shift SDV represents versus traditional automotive E/E architecture
Identify how SDV changes requirements and release practice
Discuss organizational implications of SDV adoption

title: Functional Safety Overview
summary: ISO 26262 fundamentals — ASIL classification, the safety lifecycle, and safety requirements.
description: A foundational course in automotive functional safety per ISO 26262 — hazard analysis, ASIL determination, and how safety requirements flow through the development lifecycle.
outcomes: Explain the ISO 26262 safety lifecycle end to end
Determine ASIL classification from a hazard and risk analysis
Trace safety requirements through to verification evidence

title: Automotive Cybersecurity Introduction
summary: ISO/SAE 21434 fundamentals and the cybersecurity requirements every automotive engineer should know.
description: An introduction to automotive cybersecurity engineering per ISO/SAE 21434 — threat analysis, risk assessment (TARA), and how cybersecurity requirements integrate with the rest of the development process.
outcomes: Explain the ISO/SAE 21434 cybersecurity engineering process
Run a basic threat analysis and risk assessment (TARA)
Identify where cybersecurity requirements intersect with functional and safety requirements
